claims.text: Introducing controlled nanoporosity via selective laser sintering can enhance heat transfer in high-entropy alloys used in plasma-facing reactor components.
The initial high-entropy alloy is in a dense form.
Selective laser sintering can introduce controlled nanoporosity into the high-entropy alloy.
The proposed improvement should hold from 500°C to 1000°C.
The proposed improvement should hold under mechanical loads up to 100 MPa.
The intervention produces a nanoporous structure.
Nanoporosity increases the surface area available for heat exchange.
The increased surface area improves heat-transfer capability.
Nanoporosity will improve heat-transfer capability by at least 20% relative to dense high-entropy alloys.
Current intermediate layers use dense high-entropy alloys.
Porosity above 30% may compromise structural integrity.
Specific data are lacking on the optimal nanoporosity level for balancing heat transfer and structural integrity.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 20% improvement, whereas the falsification rule only falsifies improvements of 10% or less. An outcome between greater than 10% and less than 20% would miss the hypothesis target but would not falsify it under the stated rule.
